newsitem.title: USA: Latam bond issuance sets record - ING Barings.
newsitem.headline: Latam bond issuance sets record - ING Barings.

text.p: New Latin American bond issuance surged to an all-time high in the first eight weeks of 1997, reported ING Barings in its weekly report on emerging markets.

More than US$12 billion of bonds had been issued by February 21, with the sovereigns leading the borrowing spree and accounting for $7.95 billion in debt, or two-thirds of the year-to-date total, according to Arturo Porzecanski, chief Latin America economist at ING Barings.
Corporate new issuance accounted for 28 percent of the total, compared with 21.6 percent at year-end 1996, the report said.
Argentina and Mexico were the largest issuers, it said.
"It is clear that a veritable tidal wave of investor money has washed up and settled on Latin America's shores," Porzecanski noted.
The 1996 record of $51.4 billion is more than double the previous peak of $21.9 billion set in 1993, the report said.
